content.text: No exclusivity obligation binds the Customer — the document affirmatively disclaims it.

input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no exclusivity, sole-supplier, or all-requirements obligation on Customer. Clause 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and confirms Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. Clause 2.1 reinforces this: no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and a decision not to place further Order Forms is not a breach. The only exclusivity-flavoured restriction, clause 12.4 (Vendor shall not market a service competing with Customer's analytics products), runs against Vendor and benefits us, so per the detection guidance it is not a deviation and should be retained. Searches for "exclusive", "sole", and requirements/third-party procurement language surfaced only non-exclusive licence grants, non-exclusive remedies, and exclusive jurisdiction — none imposing exclusive dealing on Customer. Preferred position met; no redline required.
